title: AP2 v0.2 human present: the user signs closed mandates on a Trusted Surface
summary: The direct mode. The merchant signs the checkout, the user approves the exact Checkout and Payment Mandates on a non-agentic Trusted Surface, the Credential Provider verifies the Payment Mandate and issues a token, the merchant and its processor verify the hash bindings, and both sides return signed receipts.

steps.label: Start shopping
steps.detail: The user asks the Shopping Agent to find and buy something. AP2 defines nothing about this exchange; the flows in the specification assume enrollment and any user credential already exist.

steps.label: Build a cart over the commerce protocol
steps.detail: The agent browses and assembles a cart. Catalog, cart and checkout calls belong to the surrounding commerce protocol, for example UCP; AP2 leaves them out of scope.

steps.label: Signed checkout (checkout_jwt); mandate required
steps.detail: The merchant creates the checkout, signs it as a JWT and says a mandate is required to continue. The specification text asks for a non-deterministic signature such as ECDSA here, while the security considerations allow a deterministic one with enough salt (issue 268).

failures.condition: The cart changes after this point
failures.outcome: The merchant will reject any mandate whose checkout_hash does not match its latest checkout_jwt.

steps.label: Fetch instrument options
steps.detail: The agent asks the Credential Provider, for example a wallet or a network, for the instruments it can use, and picks one. AP2 defines no message format for this call.

steps.label: Request approval of Checkout and Payment Mandate Content
steps.detail: The agent assembles the unsigned content of a closed Checkout Mandate and a closed Payment Mandate and hands it to a Trusted Surface. The surface is external under the User Credential model or internal under the Trusted Agent Provider model.

steps.label: Show the content; authenticate and get consent
steps.detail: The Trusted Surface renders the exact checkout and payment and authenticates the user, for example with a biometric. It must be non-agentic: no language model decides what the user sees.

failures.outcome: No mandate is signed and nothing is presented.

steps.label: Sign closed mandates with user_sk
steps.detail: The surface signs mandate.checkout.1 and mandate.payment.1. The hash of checkout_jwt appears in both (checkout_hash and transaction_id), which links them for good. Under the Trusted Agent Provider model the key belongs to the agent provider and must stay out of the agent's reach.

steps.label: Return the signed mandates
steps.detail: The surface passes both closed mandates back to the agent.

steps.label: Present the closed Payment Mandate
steps.detail: The Credential Provider verifies the mandate under the Delegate SD-JWT rules and checks its content before it releases any credential.

failures.condition: The signature or chain does not verify
failures.outcome: Payment Receipt with status Error and error invalid_credential; terminal.

failures.condition: The mandate does not approve this payment
failures.outcome: Payment Receipt with error invalid_mandate; terminal.

steps.label: Share the mandate, get a scoped credential (optional)
steps.detail: The Credential Provider may pass the Payment Mandate to the payment network and receive a purchase credential scoped to this transaction, also called a token. The network then verifies the mandate under the same rules.

steps.label: Payment token
steps.detail: The token is released only after a final Payment Mandate is verified, which limits the damage if an agent or a token is stolen.

steps.label: Token plus closed Checkout Mandate
steps.detail: The agent completes the checkout with the token and the user-signed Checkout Mandate.

failures.condition: The hash of the merchant's checkout_jwt does not equal checkout_hash
failures.outcome: The merchant returns a Checkout Receipt JWT with status Error.

failures.condition: A verification step fails for any other reason
failures.outcome: The merchant must return a Checkout Receipt JWT carrying the error.

failures.condition: The merchant does not use mandates for this action
failures.outcome: It answers mandates_not_supported in a Checkout Receipt, a signal to fall back to a non-agentic flow.

steps.label: Initiate payment with the token and the checkout_jwt hash
steps.detail: The merchant has checked the mandate against the current cart. For a pull payment it asks its processor to charge; for a push method it instead waits for confirmation that funds were sent.

steps.label: Verify the Payment Mandate inside the token
steps.detail: The processor checks that the credential is scoped to this checkout, for example by finding the closed Payment Mandate inside the token and matching its transaction_id to the checkout_jwt hash.

failures.condition: transaction_id does not match the checkout_jwt hash
failures.outcome: The payment is refused and a Payment Receipt with status Error goes back.

steps.label: Payment Receipt (also to the Credential Provider and Network)
steps.detail: The processor signs a Payment Receipt whose reference is the hash of the closed Payment Mandate.

payload.content:
# Illustrative example, spec version v0.2. Decoded view; hashes and signatures shortened.
# Payment Receipt JWT payload, signed by the Merchant Payment Processor (payment_receipt.json).
{
  "status": "Success",
  "iss": "https://processor.example",
  "iat": 1791720030,
  "reference": "k9Pq...hash-of-closed-payment-mandate",
  "payment_id": "pay_2b71",
  "psp_confirmation_id": "psp_88a1",
  "network_confirmation_id": "net_51c0"
}

steps.label: Checkout Receipt
steps.detail: The merchant signs a Checkout Receipt whose reference is the hash of the closed Checkout Mandate. With both receipts and both mandates, a dispute verifier can rebuild what the user approved.
